suggestions.assertion: The executing piece is inline or a haiku-tier agent, not sonnet/opus/fable
suggestions.reason: This assertion is ambiguous in a fixture where the acting session always self-identifies as a top-tier model ('Fable'). If 'inline' is read as an unconditional pass regardless of which model does the work, this run passes trivially -- simply by defaulting to 'I'll just do it myself,' the behavior an unguided agent falls into by default -- which would make the assertion unable to ever catch the exact failure mode (an expensive model doing 15 mechanical edits itself) that the companion with_skill run for this identical task was specifically designed to avoid (its brief explicitly says 'do not inherit the session model'). Recommend tightening the wording so 'inline' cannot be satisfied by a stated large-model session doing the work directly, e.g. 'the model tier performing the edits -- inline or delegated -- is haiku or smaller.'

suggestions.assertion: States all seven complexity scores (S, R, A, K, I, P, V) explicitly with values
suggestions.reason: Worth confirming the eval intends a hard requirement here rather than a soft one: this run reasons carefully and arrives at conclusions that map cleanly onto the rubric (e.g. its table is effectively an S-dimension scoping exercise, and its 'no verifier, no gate' reasoning is effectively K/V reasoning) but never renders them as the S/R/A/K/I/P/V notation, so it fails outright rather than partially. That is arguably the correct strict reading (the point of the skill is the shared notation itself, not just good judgment), but it is worth the eval author double-checking that intent, since 'good reasoning, wrong notation' and 'no reasoning at all' both fail identically under the current wording.

eval_feedback.overall: This run fails half the assertions, and the two failures are substantive rather than technicalities: no complexity scores are ever stated (the rubric this eval exists to test is simply absent), and no decisions.jsonl is produced at all, so there is no machine-readable record to close a feedback loop on. The one genuinely debatable call is assertion 2 (inline-on-the-session's-own-top-tier-model) -- see the suggestion above; I graded it as a fail because the run's own words identify the executor as 'Fable,' one of the tiers the assertion names as disallowed, and because the skill's own routing policy treats 'inline' as inheriting the session's tier rather than as an exemption from it.
